item.title: study title
item.description: Agreement I do not AgreeBody Upon reading the paper thoroughly and studying the neuroimaging and the description of the structural brain lesions described in this case, it became clear that the patient experienced mostly deep grey matter involvement of the brain. Therefore, it would be scientifically inaccurate to use the term leukoencephalopathy in the title. As of today, this paper has been cited 21 times already as per the Google Scholar. It behooves the journal to quickly rectify this error.

item.title: Limitations of ECG as a diagnostic tool in pulmonary embolism: A call for Guidance-Based Evaluation
item.description: Agreement I do not AgreeBody Dear editor, The author has highlighted the role of ECG in diagnosing pulmonary embolism(PE). I would like to respectfully contribute to the discussion on the diagnostic pathway for PE, particularly the limitations of relying on ECG findings. ECG changes have low sensitivity and specificity in the diagnosis of PE. item.title: Reply to: Hippocampal stroke masquerading as transient global amnesia.
item.description: Agreement I do not AgreeBody Dear Muzzamil I would like to debate that your case report represents hippocampal ischaemia/stroke [1]. One or several punctate hippocampal lesions – unilateral or bilateral – in diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) are a hallmark of transient global amnesia (TGA) [2]. In ischaemic amnesia, hippocampal lesions are non-punctate and/or extra-hippocampal [3].
